analysis_notes.notes: All 5 nodes from the 3 bechina edges are assigned to exactly one package — no orphans. The 3 non-bechina edges for reference 1019 are all type 'eitza' and correctly represent causal flows rather than shared-nature identities. The source text contains a dense cluster of bechina identifications not yet in the dataset: (1) 'יָדָיו – הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת מִצְווֹת מַעֲשִׂיּוֹת' (hands = practical commandments), (2) 'הֵם בְּחִינַת אֱמוּנָה' (practical commandments = faith), (3) 'וֶאֱמוּנָה זֶה תְּפִלָּה' (faith = prayer) — these three linked bechinas form an independent good cluster: ידיו ↔ מצוות מעשיות ↔ אמונה ↔ תפלה. Additionally, (4) Package 2 is missing תמימות ופשיטות, which the Rebbe explicitly calls a bechina of סוף דבר. Note: 'אמונה' appears in the dataset for reference 1019 only as an eitza edge (cause-node that weakens Amalek) — but within the source text it also plays a bechina role (it IS prayer; practical commandments ARE it). These are distinct relational roles. The Torah's structural argument: the evil cluster (Package 1: Amalek/philosophers/stumbling-block) is overcome by the good cluster (faith/prayer/practical commandments), which leads to the ultimate good (Package 2: תכלית/תמימות/סוף דבר). The eitza flow runs: אמונה ומצוות מעשיות → חליש את עמלק → תכלית. The bechinas within those causal nodes are what this gap analysis surfaces.
